Common reasons include:</p><ul><li>Severe decay that has damaged the tooth beyond what a filling, crown, or root canal can repair</li><li>Infection or abscess that hasn't responded to other treatments and risks spreading</li><li>Trauma or fracture that has compromised the tooth's structure below the gumline</li><li>Crowding that interferes with orthodontic treatment or proper alignment</li><li>Impacted or partially erupted teeth, including wisdom teeth, that are causing pain or pushing against neighboring teeth</li></ul><p>If you're experiencing persistent tooth pain, swelling, or sensitivity, schedule an evaluation at our Raleigh office so we can assess whether extraction is necessary or if a less invasive option will do the job.</p></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-7\"><h2>How a Tooth Extraction Works at Our Raleigh Office</h2><div class=\"source-chunk\"><p>Knowing what to expect can take a lot of the anxiety out of the experience. Here's a step-by-step look at how we handle extractions:</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      1. Exam and Imaging\n                            </h3><p>We start with a thorough examination and digital imaging to evaluate the tooth's condition, root structure, and surrounding bone. This helps us plan the safest, most efficient approach.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      2. Anesthesia and Comfort\n                            </h3><p>Before anything begins, we numb the area with a local anesthetic to ensure you don't feel pain during the procedure. If you're feeling anxious, let us know ahead of time so we can take extra steps to help you feel at ease.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      3. The Extraction\n                            </h3><p>For a simple extraction, we use specialized instruments to gently loosen the tooth and remove it. You may feel pressure, but you should not feel pain. More complex cases, such as a broken tooth or one that hasn't fully erupted, may require a surgical approach. Either way, our doctors work carefully to minimize disruption and support a fast recovery.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      4. Aftercare and Recovery\n                            </h3><p>Once the tooth is out, we'll place gauze to manage bleeding and provide detailed aftercare instructions. Most patients recover within a few days. During that time, you'll want to stick to soft foods, avoid drinking through straws, and follow our guidance on managing swelling and discomfort.</p></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-8\"><h2>A patient’s experience</h2><div class=\"source-chunk\"><blockquote><p>\"Had an amazing experience at this dentist office! All of the staff is so welcoming, kind, and knowledgeable. Dr. Gajjar is the best dentist I have ever had. He is so good at explaining what is going on with my teeth and what I need to do about them. I’ve been a patient of Dr. Gajjar for a couple of years and am so happy that he’s now at this location in Raleigh!\" — Divya, <a href=\"https://maps.app.goo.gl/jQnE4mYqVt8qRCKeA\">5-Star Review</a></p></blockquote></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-9\"><h2>Frequently Asked Questions About Tooth Extraction in Raleigh, NC</h2><div class=\"faq\"><details><summary>Does a tooth extraction hurt?</summary><p>No. We use local anesthesia to completely numb the area before starting. Most patients feel only pressure during the procedure, not pain. After the numbness wears off, mild soreness is normal and can typically be managed with over-the-counter pain relievers and the aftercare steps we provide.</p></details><details><summary>How long does recovery take?</summary><p>Most patients feel significantly better within two to three days. Full healing of the extraction site generally takes one to two weeks, depending on the complexity of the procedure. We'll give you a clear recovery timeline and check in as needed.</p></details><details><summary>What are my options for replacing an extracted tooth?</summary><p>We can place a bridge or a crown supported by a <a href=\"/services/dental-implants/\">dental implant</a>. Your dentist will discuss replacement options with you before your extraction appointment so you have a plan in place. In many cases, we can begin the restorative process shortly after the site has healed.</p></details><details><summary>Do you remove wisdom teeth?</summary><p>Yes. With proper care and routine checkups, they can last 20 years or more, and many patients enjoy results that last a lifetime.</p></details><details><summary>Is the implant procedure painful?</summary><p>The procedure itself isn’t painful. We use local anesthesia to keep you comfortable throughout treatment. For patients who feel anxious, we offer oral anxiolysis, a safe, simple medication option that helps you feel calm and relaxed during your visit. Mild soreness afterward is common and typically easy to manage.</p></details><details><summary>Will my insurance cover dental implants?</summary><p>Most dental insurance plans don't cover the implant post itself, but they may help with related procedures like exams, imaging, extractions, or the final crown. We’ll walk you through your benefits.</p></details><details><summary>What if I’m missing several teeth?</summary><p>Implants can replace a single tooth or support larger restorations like bridges or dentures. Full-arch implant solutions are available for patients who are missing most or all of their teeth.</p></details><details><summary>How long does the dental implant process take from start to finish?</summary><p>It varies by patient. After placement, the implant typically needs three to six months to fuse with the jawbone before the final crown, bridge, or denture goes on. If you need prep work like bone grafting or extractions first, that adds some time. We'll give you a realistic timeline during your consultation so there aren't any surprises.</p></details><details><summary>What happens if I don&#x27;t replace a missing tooth?</summary><p>The teeth around the gap can start shifting, and the jawbone underneath begins to deteriorate without a root to support it. Over time that can change your bite, affect how you chew, and make future dental work more complicated. Implants are one of the few options that actually prevent that bone loss because the titanium post acts like a natural tooth root.</p></details></div></section></div></div></main><section class=\"closing\"><span class=\"eyebrow\">Raleigh Comprehensive &amp; Cosmetic Dentistry</span><h2>Schedule an<br>Appointment</h2><div class=\"actions\"><a class=\"button dark\" href=\"/contact/\">Request an Appointment</a><a class=\"text-link\" href=\"tel:+19198283775\">(919) 828-3775</a></div></section><footer><div class=\"footer-top\"><a class=\"brand\" href=\"/\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">r.</span><span>raleigh<span class=\"brand-small\">comprehensive & cosmetic dentistry</span></span></a><div><p>119 North Boylan Avenue<br>Raleigh, NC 27603</p><a href=\"/locations/raleigh-office/\">Hours & directions</a></div><div><a href=\"/services/\">Explore our care</a><a href=\"/meet-the-team/\">Meet the team</a><a href=\"/our-approach/\">Our approach & technology</a><a href=\"/photogallery/\">Smile gallery</a></div><div><a href=\"/new-patients/\">New patients</a><a href=\"/new-patients/#payment\">Insurance & financing</a><a href=\"/contact/\">Contact us</a></div></div><div class=\"footer-bottom\"><span>© 2026 Raleigh Comprehensive & Cosmetic Dentistry</span><a href=\"/privacy-policy/\">Privacy policy</a><a href=\"/site-map/\">Site map</a></div><p class=\"fineprint\">Treatment recommendations and results vary by individual. Whether you’re ready to start right away or need time to heal first, we’re here to support you in the long run.</p></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-10\"><h2>Emergency dentistry FAQs</h2><div class=\"faq\"><details><summary>Can I come in without being an existing patient?</summary><p>Yes. We welcome new and returning patients for emergency care. You don’t need to be an established patient to receive same-day treatment.</p></details><details><summary>What if I’m not sure it’s an emergency?</summary><p>If you’re in pain, have swelling, or feel something isn’t right, call us. Our team can help assess your symptoms and recommend next steps.</p></details><details><summary>Will I need to come back for follow-up care?</summary><p>In some cases, yes. We may place a temporary restoration or begin treatment that requires a second visit to complete. If so, we’ll explain everything clearly.</p></details><details><summary>How much does emergency dental care cost in Raleigh?</summary><p>Cost depends on the type of treatment you need, and we won't know that until we see you. What we can tell you is that we don't require full payment upfront. You'll only pay your estimated portion at the time of your visit. Our financial consultant can review your insurance and walk you through financing options like CareCredit before any treatment begins.</p></details><details><summary>Can you treat a dental emergency if I have dental anxiety?</summary><p>Yes. We offer oral anxiolysis, a safe, simple medication that helps you stay calm and relaxed during your visit. Local anesthesia keeps the actual treatment comfortable. If anxiety has kept you from seeking care in the past, let us know when you call so we can plan accordingly.</p></details></div></section></div></div></main><section class=\"closing\"><span class=\"eyebrow\">Raleigh Comprehensive &amp; Cosmetic Dentistry</span><h2>Schedule an<br>Appointment</h2><div class=\"actions\"><a class=\"button dark\" href=\"/contact/\">Request an Appointment</a><a class=\"text-link\" href=\"tel:+19198283775\">(919) 828-3775</a></div></section><footer><div class=\"footer-top\"><a class=\"brand\" href=\"/\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">r.</span><span>raleigh<span class=\"brand-small\">comprehensive & cosmetic dentistry</span></span></a><div><p>119 North Boylan Avenue<br>Raleigh, NC 27603</p><a href=\"/locations/raleigh-office/\">Hours & directions</a></div><div><a href=\"/services/\">Explore our care</a><a href=\"/meet-the-team/\">Meet the team</a><a href=\"/our-approach/\">Our approach & technology</a><a href=\"/photogallery/\">Smile gallery</a></div><div><a href=\"/new-patients/\">New patients</a><a href=\"/new-patients/#payment\">Insurance & financing</a><a href=\"/contact/\">Contact us</a></div></div><div class=\"footer-bottom\"><span>© 2026 Raleigh Comprehensive & Cosmetic Dentistry</span><a href=\"/privacy-policy/\">Privacy policy</a><a href=\"/site-map/\">Site map</a></div><p class=\"fineprint\">Treatment recommendations and results vary by individual. Here's how a typical cleaning appointment works at our office:</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      Comprehensive Exam\n                            </h3><p>Your visit starts with a thorough evaluation of your teeth, gums, and overall oral health. Your dental hygienist will check for signs of decay, gum disease, and any other conditions that may need attention.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      Professional Scaling\n                            </h3><p>Your hygienist will use specialized instruments to carefully remove plaque and tartar buildup from the surfaces of your teeth and along the gumline. This is the step that targets the hardened deposits that regular brushing and flossing can't remove.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      Polishing and Flossing\n                            </h3><p>Once scaling is complete, your teeth are polished to remove surface stains and leave them feeling smooth. A professional flossing follows to ensure every space between your teeth is clean.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      Oral Cancer Screening\n                            </h3><p>As part of every cleaning visit, your Raleigh dentist performs a quick, painless screening for any signs of oral cancer. Early detection is one of the most important benefits of keeping up with your routine visits.</p></div><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>\n                      Personalized Guidance\n                            </h3><p>Before you leave, your hygienist will share tips tailored to your specific needs, whether that's adjusting your brushing technique, recommending a toothbrush, or flagging an area to watch between visits.</p></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-7\"><h2>A patient’s experience</h2><div class=\"source-chunk\"><h3>“Welcomed and well taken care of.”</h3><blockquote><p>\"As someone who fears dentistry, Doctor J and Doctor Gajjar made me feel comfortable, welcomed and well-taken care of. I went to my first visit two weeks ago, and immediately scheduled my follow up for this week.\" — Nelsy, <a href=\"https://maps.app.goo.gl/yJGbBEb2Lg7Y5HWY8\">5-Star Review</a></p></blockquote></div></section><section class=\"source-section\" id=\"section-8\"><h2>Teeth cleaning FAQs</h2><div class=\"faq\"><details><summary>How often should I get my teeth cleaned?</summary><p>Most dental professionals recommend a teeth cleaning every six months. However, some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, especially those with a history of gum disease, heavy tartar buildup, or other ongoing oral health concerns. During your visit, your dentist will recommend a schedule based on your individual needs.</p></details><details><summary>What&#x27;s the difference between a regular cleaning and a deep cleaning?</summary><p>A regular cleaning focuses on the surfaces of your teeth and just above the gumline. It's designed for patients with generally healthy gums. A deep cleaning, also known as scaling and root planing, goes below the gumline to remove tartar and bacteria from the roots of your teeth. Deep cleanings are typically recommended for patients showing signs of gum disease.</p></details><details><summary>Do teeth cleanings hurt?</summary><p>For most patients, a routine cleaning involves little to no discomfort. Our team uses a gentle approach and will check in with you throughout the appointment. If you have sensitive teeth or gums, or if it's been a while since your last visit, let us know ahead of time so we can take extra steps to keep you comfortable.</p></details><details><summary>Can I get other dental work done at the same appointment?</summary><p>In many cases, yes. Because we offer a full range of general, restorative, and cosmetic services under one roof, we can often address additional needs during the same visit or coordinate follow-up care without referring you elsewhere. Just let us know what's on your mind when you schedule, and we'll plan accordingly.</p><p>Schedule your next teeth cleaning with us today. As your dentist in Raleigh, NC, we look forward to helping you maintain a healthy, confident smile.</p></details></div></section></div></div></main><section class=\"closing\"><span class=\"eyebrow\">Raleigh Comprehensive &amp; Cosmetic Dentistry</span><h2>Schedule an<br>Appointment</h2><div class=\"actions\"><a class=\"button dark\" href=\"/contact/\">Request an Appointment</a><a class=\"text-link\" href=\"tel:+19198283775\">(919) 828-3775</a></div></section><footer><div class=\"footer-top\"><a class=\"brand\" href=\"/\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">r.</span><span>raleigh<span class=\"brand-small\">comprehensive & cosmetic dentistry</span></span></a><div><p>119 North Boylan Avenue<br>Raleigh, NC 27603</p><a href=\"/locations/raleigh-office/\">Hours & directions</a></div><div><a href=\"/services/\">Explore our care</a><a href=\"/meet-the-team/\">Meet the team</a><a href=\"/our-approach/\">Our approach & technology</a><a href=\"/photogallery/\">Smile gallery</a></div><div><a href=\"/new-patients/\">New patients</a><a href=\"/new-patients/#payment\">Insurance & financing</a><a href=\"/contact/\">Contact us</a></div></div><div class=\"footer-bottom\"><span>© 2026 Raleigh Comprehensive & Cosmetic Dentistry</span><a href=\"/privacy-policy/\">Privacy policy</a><a href=\"/site-map/\">Site map</a></div><p class=\"fineprint\">Treatment recommendations and results vary by individual.
